_readme: Scenario set for the laws-of-ux skill. Three measured quantities: TRIGGERING (should the skill fire from its description alone?), ROUTING (does the index lead to the right law?), and LIFT (does the skill beat an unaided model?). Positives list every acceptable slug in expected_refs. Negatives are near-misses that deliberately share vocabulary with a law but need something else. Scenarios carrying a `trap` are the lift set: `trap` records what an unaided model reliably answers instead, and `trap_refs` the law it wrongly reaches for. A scenario only counts as lift if the unaided answer hits the trap AND the skilled answer reaches expected_refs.

scenarios.prompt: We're designing a navigation menu. How many items is too many before it becomes hard to use?
scenarios.trap: Cites Miller's Law and a 7±2 cap on menu items. That is the canonical misapplication: Miller's limit governs what must be HELD in working memory, not what may be visible. A visible list is not held. Option-set size is Hick's Law.

scenarios.prompt: This signup form has 14 fields and feels bloated. Simplify it.
scenarios.trap: Proposes deleting fields without asking where the work goes. Removing a field the system could infer is real simplification; removing one because it looks cluttered pushes the work onto the user. Tesler's check — where did the complexity go? — is the discriminator.

scenarios.prompt: Nobody clicks our main call-to-action even though it's right there at the top.
scenarios.trap: Reaches for copywriting or colour changes on the button itself, without noticing that contrast is a property of the SET. If everything nearby is already emphasised, making this one louder cannot work.

scenarios.prompt: Our tool's config file has grown to about 40 options and new users say they don't know where to start.
scenarios.trap: Suggests better documentation for the 40 options rather than treating the option count itself as the defect. Documentation does not reduce a logarithmic decision cost.

scenarios.prompt: Our CLI tool goes quiet for about 30 seconds while it works, then dumps the full result. Users say it feels broken.
scenarios.trap: Suggests a spinner and stops there. The threshold is about holding attention — streaming partial results and stating intent up front buy back attention that a spinner does not.

scenarios.prompt: Our service log tags nearly every line as ERROR and the on-call engineers have stopped reading it.
scenarios.trap: Treats it as a log-level configuration task only, missing that emphasis inflation destroys the channel it runs on — the same mechanism as five 'primary' buttons on one screen.
